sights.n: SFO Louis A. Turpen Aviation Museum & Library
sights.address: International Terminal Main Hall, Departures Level (pre-security), San Francisco International Airport, San Francisco, CA 94128
sights.w: The only accredited museum inside an airport: a free, pre-security gallery built as a replica 1930s passenger terminal, tracing West Coast and Pacific commercial aviation with aircraft models, airline memorabilia and photographs. Open daily 10am-4:30pm, no ticket needed.

sights.n: Sign Hill (SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO THE INDUSTRIAL CITY letters)
sights.address: Sign Hill Park, Poplar Ave, South San Francisco, CA 94080
sights.w: The city's Hollywood-style hillside sign: white concrete letters 48-65 ft tall spelling SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO THE INDUSTRIAL CITY, built in 1929 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places. A 30-acre park with ~2 miles of trails climbs to the letters and bay views.

sights.n: San Bruno Mountain State & County Park
sights.w: A rare island of native coastal-scrub habitat rising straight off the bay's edge above Daly City, Brisbane and South SF. Summit and ridge trails deliver 360-degree views from the Golden Gate to the Santa Cruz Mountains; home to endangered Mission blue butterflies.

sights.n: Sweeney Ridge (San Francisco Bay Discovery Site)
sights.address: Sneath Lane Trailhead, Sneath Ln, San Bruno, CA 94066
sights.w: GGNRA ridgeline between San Bruno and Pacifica where the Portola expedition first sighted San Francisco Bay on Nov 4, 1769 - a registered historic landmark. Trails from Sneath Lane and Skyline College climb to the discovery-site monument and ocean-to-bay panoramas.

sights.address: 1651 Coyote Point Dr, San Mateo, CA 94401
sights.w: A hands-on science-and-wildlife museum inside Coyote Point Recreation Area, overlooking the bay: live native-animal exhibits (raptors, foxes, bobcat) and interactive natural-science galleries. Surrounded by shoreline, eucalyptus groves and beach in a regional park.

sights.n: San Mateo Central Park & Japanese Garden
sights.w: A hidden strolling garden designed by Nagao Sakurai of the Imperial Palace of Tokyo, with a granite pagoda, teahouse, koi pond and bamboo grove, tucked inside downtown San Mateo's Central Park. Free admission.

sights.address: Beach Blvd (at Santa Rosa Ave), Pacifica, CA 94044
sights.w: A 1,140-ft concrete pier jutting into the Pacific off Sharp Park Beach - a free, no-license fishing and crabbing spot famous for salmon and Dungeness crab runs, with wide-open sunset and whale-watching views straight out over the ocean.

sights.address: Devil's Slide Trail, CA-1 (Cabrillo Hwy), Pacifica, CA 94044
sights.w: A 1.3-mile paved clifftop trail on a former stretch of Highway 1, reopened in 2014 after the Tom Lantos Tunnels rerouted the road. It hugs a sheer cliff face hundreds of feet above the surf with sweeping ocean, seabird and gray-whale views. Parking lots at both ends.

A 110-acre GGNRA headland in Pacifica: a short climb up the Mori Point Peak loop delivers a dramatic bluff-top view over the ocean, Sharp Park Beach and the coastline, through wildflower meadows and wetlands that shelter the endangered red-legged frog and San Francisco garter snake.

The point where the San Andreas Fault meets the Pacific - the closest land to the epicenter of the 1906 earthquake, its tarmac visibly rippled by the fault. Cliffside 'laminar flow' winds make it one of the Bay Area's premier hang-gliding and paragliding launches, with big coastal sunsets.

sights.n: Burlingame Museum of PEZ Memorabilia — CLOSED
sights.w: A beloved roadside oddity that displayed one of the world's largest PEZ dispenser collections plus banned/rare pieces and the 'world's largest PEZ dispenser.' Permanently closed in July 2019 - kept here for the record; do not visit.

food.dish: baked BBQ pork buns, har gow, roast duck with truffle oil
food.w: With Millbrae's famous dim sum halls (Hong Kong Flower Lounge, Zen Peninsula, Asian Pearl) all now shuttered, this Michelin Guide-listed Cantonese hall is the survivor - cart-service lunch dim sum known for its baked (not steamed) BBQ pork buns and roast duck with truffle oil.

The flagship turo-turo ('point-point') of Daly City, the largest Filipino community in the U.S.: point at steaming trays of crispy lechon kawali and peanutty kare-kare, plus grilled BBQ skewers. Cash-only, takeout, a decades-old local institution.

food.address: 2055 Gellert Blvd, Ste 5, Daly City, CA 94015
food.w: A low-key Daly City sit-down spot (walls of '80s movie and boxing posters) doing sharp renditions of Filipino classics; the must-order is the crispy, citrusy sizzling sisig, with lumpiang Shanghai close behind. Featured on KQED's Check, Please! Bay Area.

A family-run Filipino bakery on Top of the Hill baking pandesal since 1977 - warm rolls out of the oven from 5-7am, plus ensaymada and bibingka. A generational Daly City institution recently kept in the family by three cousins.

food.address: 599 Railroad Ave, South San Francisco, CA 94080
food.w: The Bay Area's living Basque hearth: founded 1982 by the region's sheepherding diaspora, it serves hearty family-style Basque dinners - lamb, duck, seafood - and the classic Picon Punch, beside an indoor pilota (jai alai) court. A genuine cultural institution, open to all.

food.address: 115 De Anza Blvd, San Mateo, CA 94402
food.w: San Mateo's sole Michelin-starred restaurant: a 16-seat strip-mall counter where chef Katsuhiro Yamasaki serves a monthly-changing nine-course kaiseki built on California-seasonal ingredients. Reservations vanish instantly.

food.dish: garlic pork (tonkotsu) ramen with fried whole garlic
food.address: 805 S B St, San Mateo, CA 94401
food.w: A 24-seat downtown San Mateo ramen shop with a line half an hour before it opens: garlic-pork, soybean or soy broths dialed from mild to extra-spicy, loaded with fried whole garlic. Come early - they run out of broth.

The first Indian restaurant in California to win a Michelin star (held 2016-2021); chef Ajay Walia's modern South-Indian coastal cooking - dosa, chutney prawns, Railway pepper, biryani - reopened on Burlingame Ave in 2024 after a hiatus.

The German beer-hall co-founded by cookbook author J. Kenji Lopez-Alt, a downtown San Mateo fixture since 2018 known for house sausages, currywurst and pretzels. Permanently closed Sept 27, 2025 - kept here for the record (basement bar Wunderbar may continue).
